rows.synopsis: A pregnant Tuarangisaurus is in distress, and her young calf can sense it, as she struggles through the shallows. Meanwhile a Tyrannosaurus rex family swims to an offshore island and thousands of pterosaur hatchlings take their first flight.
rows.situation: On a dangerous coast, a T. rex father leads his youngsters on their first swim past the biggest predator in the sea, baby pterosaurs launch from a cliff into a sky full of hunters, and a young Tuarangisaurus calf stays close to his pregnant mother when she gets into trouble in the shallows.
rows.coping: The T. rex father positions himself between his brood and the mosasaur, the hatchlings time their first flight when one brave youngster finally leaps, and the calf stays with his mother and follows the family group until the danger passes.

rows.per_story_synopsis: A father T. rex brings his last four youngsters on a risky first crossing to a turtle nursery island, and every one of them has to learn fast that staying close is what keeps you alive.

rows.synopsis: Above the deserts of North Africa, aerial combat ensues as male Barbaridactylus pterosaurs compete for the attention of females. In this dry, unforgiving habitat, Dinosaurs of every size and shape must use all their skills.
rows.situation: In the harshest dry places on the planet, a giant Dreadnoughtus bull fights challengers for his place at the center of a mating gathering, a tiny Mononykus with a super-sensitive hearing hunts termites and must adapt when rare rain transforms her desert overnight, and male Barbaridactylus duel in the air over canyon display grounds.
rows.coping: The young Dreadnoughtus challenger keeps fighting until the old bull is worn down, Mononykus takes bold chances to grab fleeting meals and adapts when the landscape changes, and animals at the crowded oasis take turns and wait their turn.
rows.notes: script_vs_synopsis: the script carries the Dreadnoughtus endurance fight, the Mononykus facial-disc hearing and termite claw, the desert storm transformation and the oasis queue, all far richer than the synopsis; high confidence.

rows.per_story_synopsis: In a desert where one wrong move ends everything, a giant old champion holds his stage against a younger challenger, and a pint-sized hunter with ears like a radar dish shows that small can be mighty.

rows.synopsis: With its feathered body and duck bill, the eight-ton Deinocheirus wades through the rivers of Asia. Meanwhile, an aging Tyrannosaurus rex seeks a mate, and a mother Quetzalcoatlus fights to protect her eggs.
rows.situation: Along rivers and flooded plains, an old battle-scarred T. rex who was hurt hunting a Triceratops meets a female who likes his scars, a Velociraptor pack uses a roaring waterfall to sneak up on a sleeping pterosaur colony, and a mother Quetzalcoatlus loses most of her twelve eggs when an older female raids her nest.
rows.coping: The old T. rex lets river water help clean his wounds and shows his gentle side to win a partner, the Quetzalcoatlus mother drives off the raider and guards her three remaining eggs with everything she has, and the Velociraptors work as a team where one alone would fail.
rows.notes: script_vs_synopsis: the script carries the nuzzling courtship, the waterfall ambush plan, the dung-fertilizer joke and the nest raid that leaves three eggs of twelve, none visible in the synopsis; high confidence.
rows.script_source: Gestdown (Subvault): Prehistoric Planet s01e03
rows.per_story_synopsis: A mother giant pterosaur lays twelve eggs and loses nine in one raid, then keeps guarding the last three, because the family you still have is worth everything.

rows.synopsis: Within the snow-covered forest, a tense standoff develops between ancient rivals. Meanwhile, the sun rises in the far north for the first time in months and a herd of Olorotitan dinosaurs raise their young.
rows.situation: After three months of polar night, a small feathered dromaeosaur family must work as a team to take on big prey, a hadrosaur herd faces a chaotic river crossing that separates parents from young, and Olorotitan mothers raise babies on warm volcanic ground while mosquitoes swarm every summer.
rows.coping: The dromaeosaurs only succeed by sticking together, hadrosaur parents keep their young close and re-form the herd after the crossing scatters them, and the Olorotitan colony returns year after year to the same warm nesting ground.
rows.notes: script_vs_synopsis: the script carries the first-sunrise timing, the Ornithomimus nest-material thieves and the mosquito plague, all absent from the synopsis; high confidence.

rows.per_story_synopsis: When the sun finally returns after a long polar night, hunters who spent the dark months barely surviving have one brief spring to try again, and everything depends on teamwork.

rows.synopsis: A journey through an underground cave in North America turns perilous when a young Triceratops is separated from his family. Elsewhere, fires break out in the forests, and animals must decide whether to stay or flee.
rows.situation: In the great forests, a young Triceratops follows his family into a pitch-black cave to lick protective clay and briefly gets lost, a male Carnotaurus tidies a private stage to impress a much bigger female, and when lightning starts a forest fire an Edmontosaurus mother refuses to abandon her babies and keeps them one step ahead of the flames.
rows.coping: The calf sticks close to his family in the dark until they reach the clay lick, the Carnotaurus male keeps trying his tiny-arm display even after failing once, and the Edmontosaurus mother stays calm and keeps moving with her young until the fire burns out.
rows.notes: script_vs_synopsis: the script carries the clay-lick antidote, the 2000-degree fire, the smoke parasite trick and the charcoal-eating ankylosaur, all absent from the synopsis; high confidence.

rows.per_story_synopsis: A little Triceratops gets lost in total darkness inside a cave and finds his family again, and a dinosaur mother leads her babies through a burning forest, never leaving one behind.

rows.synopsis: On a small island, a monumental display takes place as the giant Hatzegopteryx reveals his gentle side in the hopes of attracting a mate. Meanwhile, danger lurks in the aftermath of a tropical storm.
rows.situation: On the islands of southern Europe, tiny Zalmoxes castaways ride storm debris out to sea hoping to start a new population, Tethyshadros calves escape giant Hatzegopteryx hunters by standing perfectly still, a Simosuchus fends off a hungry Majungasaurus from inside his burrow, and one giant pterosaur male stages a courtship display to win a female.
rows.coping: The castaways take the risky swim to a bigger raft together, the calves freeze and stay still instead of running, the Simosuchus blocks his burrow with his armored back, and the young hadrosaurs are reunited with their mother once the hunters move on.

rows.per_story_synopsis: Marooned little dinosaurs learn that sometimes the bravest move is standing perfectly still, and one lonely castaway swims for a bigger raft to start a whole new life on a distant island.

rows.synopsis: Trudging through a scorching desert, two young Tarchia find relief at an oasis in the company of a fellow ankylosaur. Meanwhile, a family of Velociraptors must persevere through a challenging summer.
rows.situation: In volcanic badlands, mother isisaurs cross a poisonous gas blanket to lay eggs in a warm crater, Corythoraptor fathers shade their nests through searing heat while an egg-thief teaches her own chicks how to crack a stolen egg, young Tarchia face a huge adult at a crowded oasis, and hundreds of newly hatched babies trek across the lava to reach the forest.
rows.coping: The Corythoraptor fathers take turns so a neighbor always keeps watch, the young Tarchia hold their ground until reinforcements arrive and the adult decides to share, and the baby isisaurs stick together through hot springs and predators until they reach the safety of the forest.
rows.notes: script_vs_synopsis: the script carries the gas-blanket nesting journey, the neighborhood watch of nesting males, the egg-thief teaching her chicks and the hatchling trek, all far richer than the synopsis; high confidence.

rows.per_story_synopsis: Fathers take turns shading each other's nests in the blistering heat, and two young armored dinosaurs learn that having a friend with a club tail makes all the difference at a crowded watering hole.

rows.synopsis: In a drought-stricken basin where much has perished, an old Pachycephalosaurus is challenged for control of his herd by a younger rival. Meanwhile, in the great swamps, a pack of T. rex uses the cover of darkness to hunt.
rows.situation: In shrinking wetlands, a young azhdarchid pterosaur practices her wobbly first flights over water full of predators, a young Austroraptor learns to grab leftover scraps while the big fishers squabble, a devil toad hunts for a mate whose singing spot keeps getting stomped by sauropods, and a young pachycephalosaur challenges the herd leader and wins, only to pay with exile.
rows.coping: The young pterosaur keeps practicing until her wings are strong enough, the Austroraptor waits patiently and snatches his chance when two adults fight, and the young herd leader learns that winning a fight does not make the hard season easier.
rows.notes: script_vs_synopsis: the script carries the maiden-flight lesson, the leftover-scrap strategy, the Beelzebufo footprint pools and the T. rex teamwork ambush, all absent from the synopsis; high confidence.
rows.script_source: Gestdown (Subvault): Prehistoric Planet s2e3
rows.per_story_synopsis: A baby flying giant has to get her takeoff just right or she lands in the water where the hunters wait, and she keeps trying until one flight finally clears the swamp.

rows.synopsis: Deep beneath the water's surface, the world's largest predator, the Mosasaurus, lies in wait. Meanwhile, baby ammonites escape a drying rock pool, and giant elasmosaurs face the ocean's most fearsome hunter.
rows.situation: In the prehistoric seas, tiny Phosphorosaurus hides by day and hunts lantern fish by night, ammonite babies trapped in a drying rock pool push together as one living tide to reach the sea, a young and inexperienced elasmosaur meets the enormous ambush hunter Mosasaurus, and Morturneria calves meet sea ice for the first time in the polar winter.
rows.coping: The ammonite babies escape by working together, each pushing the one in front, the Phosphorosaurus waits for nightfall when it is safe to hunt, and the Morturneria mothers guide their calves between the gaps in the ice to breathe.

rows.per_story_synopsis: Thousands of baby ammonites are trapped in a puddle that is drying out, and no one can save them until they push together as one and ride a tiny living tide back to the sea.

rows.synopsis: Not many can intimidate North America's top predator, T. rex, whose size and bite make it a terrifying force. Meanwhile, an elderly Alamosaurus draws his last breaths, and a Nanuqsaurus mother hunts for her young in the far north.
rows.situation: Across a changing continent, a seventy-year-old Alamosaurus reaches the end of his long life and giants contest his carcass, a Triceratops veteran proves experience beats a young rival's perfect horns, a Pectinodon father feeds his family at a toxic lake's fly bonanza, and an Arctic Nanuqsaurus mother keeps hunting through freezing winds because her cubs need her.
rows.coping: The old Alamosaurus is mourned by the pace of the herd moving on and remembered through his many offspring, the young Triceratops accepts that his battle scars may win a mate next season, and the Nanuqsaurus mother uses every failed hunt as a lesson and never gives up on feeding her cubs.

rows.per_story_synopsis: A seventy-year-old giant reaches the end of his long life on the shore, and far to the north a mother keeps hunting through the snow because her cubs cannot wait.

rows.synopsis: In a world covered in ice, woolly mammoths and saber-toothed cats fight to survive. A mother mammoth gives birth in a blizzard, and cave bears defend their cubs from lions deep underground.
rows.situation: At minus fifty degrees, a mother mammoth goes into labor alone in the first blizzard of winter and her herd forms a living shield around her and her newborn calf, cave lions stalk bear cubs a mile deep inside a warm cave city, a shaggy sloth family takes life slowly to save energy, and an elderly blind rhino gets lost in an attack until the herd closes ranks around her.
rows.coping: The mammoth herd huddles into a shield and the celebration at sunrise comes because they held together, the mother bear puts herself in the front line after the lion raid, and the rhino herd wall of horns reunites the oldest and the youngest.
rows.notes: script_vs_synopsis: the script carries the newborn calf rescue, the underground animal metropolis, the double-sabered young saber-tooth and the vole's snow tunnels, none visible in the synopsis; high confidence.

rows.per_story_synopsis: A mother mammoth gives birth alone in a blizzard, and her family arrives just in time to huddle into a shield around her baby, because in the Ice Age nobody survives alone.

rows.synopsis: As sea levels drop and continents shift, animals begin migrating to unknown territories. A giant short-faced bear stakes his claim in a new land, and a baby armadillo journeys with his mother to find water.
rows.situation: With falling seas joining continents, a giant short-faced bear walks into South America and claims a wild-dog kill with sheer presence, a giant ground sloth keeps trying new ways to crack cannonball fruit, a baby armadillo and his resourceful mother cross the scrublands to find water past a bad-tempered mammoth, and a dwarf Stegodon baby learns never to stray from her mother when giant storks hunt island babies.
rows.coping: The short-faced bear wins his new home by standing his ground, the sloth keeps trying until a strategy works, the armadillo mother sniffs out water and waits out the mammoths, and the Stegodon baby runs for the tangled roots and reaches her mother.
rows.notes: script_vs_synopsis: the script carries the cannonball fruit, the crocodile-scare at the water hole and the outsmarted Smilodon brothers, all absent from the synopsis; high confidence.

rows.per_story_synopsis: New lands are full of strangers, and a baby armadillo depends entirely on his mother's good nose for water, while island babies learn the hard way to stay close to mama.

rows.synopsis: With much of the planet's water supply frozen, rock-climbing sloths and marsupial lions fight for survival in a world of expanding deserts. A Diprotodon herd gets a bold new leader, and giant moas search for mates.
rows.situation: In the dried-out south, a mother sloth climbs a mile-high mountain to reach the only leaves while her baby waits in the cave, the old Diprotodon leader dies and her daughter takes over the herd and digs water from a dry riverbed everyone else had given up on, marsupial lion cubs wait out a hungry season until their mother perfects an ambush, and a small male moa must look as small as possible to win a ten-foot-tall mate.
rows.coping: The new Diprotodon leader digs where no one else thought to dig and saves the herd, the mother sloth keeps climbing despite the hunting birds, and the marsupial lion mother drags her kill all the way home to her waiting cub.
rows.notes: script_vs_synopsis: the script carries the mirage water hole, the wedge-tailed eagles, the moa courtship rules and the Megalania chase, all absent from the synopsis; high confidence.

rows.per_story_synopsis: When the herd's water hole turns out to be a mirage, the new young leader digs into the dry riverbed anyway, and her persistence finds water nobody else believed was there.

rows.synopsis: Giant herd animals thrive with the expansion of the grasslands, dominating the vast plains. A lonely Gigantopithecus searches for a companion as his forest home shrinks, and mammoths use their feet to hear distant rain.
rows.situation: As grasslands spread, a giant rhino soothes her tick troubles in a steaming mud spa, enormous otters claim the African plains, the last Gigantopithecus calls across his vanishing forest for a mate who never answers, a giant armadillo risks a duel with a heavier rival for a chance at love, and a mammoth herd hears distant rain through their feet just before a dust storm takes a calf too young to cover his own nose.
rows.coping: The rhino shares the spa and swaps news with other grazers, the Gigantopithecus uses his deep knowledge of the forest to scrape by when fruit grows scarce, and the mammoth leader listens with her feet and leads the herd mile after mile until the water comes.
rows.notes: script_vs_synopsis: the script carries the mud-spa information exchange, the giant otter takeover, the ant-dipping fishing trick and the calf lost in the dust storm, none visible in the synopsis; high confidence.

rows.per_story_synopsis: The last of the giant apes calls across a shrinking forest and no one answers, while a mammoth herd learns that water can be heard through your feet if you stand still and listen.

rows.synopsis: Rising temperatures mean every habitat on the planet is transforming, and for the animals of the Ice Age it is the beginning of the end. Saber-toothed cats track mammoths, sea cows graze on new kelp, and giant deer outrun hyenas.
